wiki_text: On September 17-18, 2025, Asterion Industrial Partners announced it had acquired a 25% stake in 'FluxDune', a holding company, translating to an indirect stake of roughly 15% in Dunkerque LNG (operator of Dunkirk LNG Terminal). Per Fluxys and Asterion's own disclosures, current ownership is framed as two consortia: a 61% consortium comprising Fluxys, Asterion Industrial Partners, and Credit Agricole Assurances; and a 39% consortium of Korean investors led by IPM Group with Samsung Asset Management. Previous shareholders EDF and TotalEnergies are no longer listed as owners but remain customers under long-term contracts. A full, itemized percentage reconciliation against GEM's existing Parent field was not found -- see qa note.

The Le Havre FSRU (Cape Ann, chartered by TotalEnergies) was retired in early 2026 after the Rouen Administrative Court ruled in October 2025 that the government must revoke the decree authorizing the terminal, on grounds that the energy-emergency justification (tied to the 2022 post-invasion gas-supply concerns) no longer existed. The ruling followed legal challenges from environmental organizations questioning the terminal's necessity and its environmental impact. France's Economy Minister set May 8, 2026 as the formal deadline to end operations (order signed Dec 12, 2025), but the Cape Ann vessel departed Le Havre ahead of that, on January 20-21, 2026. The vessel (IMO 9390680) is owned by a consortium of Hoegh Evi (50%), Mitsui O.S.K. Lines/MOL (48.5%), and Tokyo LNG Tanker (1.5%).
